title: PR mimi-room-policy#40: strict subset forbids a call containing the whole Group DM
description:
Step 2 of decision mimid-1wgh.109. Our own issue
ietf-wg-mimi/mimi-room-policy#40 is open and unanswered; this turns it
into a PR, which is cheap and correct whatever happens to calls.

THE DEFECT, as #40 states it: room-policy §5 (txt L533) requires a
parent-dependent room's participants to be a STRICT subset of the
parent's, and §5 L542 gives as its example "A room can be both
fixed_membership and parent_dependent, for example, for room used for a
multi-media call of clients in a Group DM". A call with everyone in the
Group DM has the same participant set, not a strict subset, so the rule
forbids the document's own example. L530's "Only a single
fixed-membership room can exist for any unique set of participants"
collides with it too, since a call room for the whole DM would duplicate
the DM's set.

#40 already proposes the fix: "subset" in place of "strict subset", and
exempting parent-dependent rooms from the single-room rule.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKED, and worth saying in the PR: working
out where a MIMI-backed call's media keys come from (bead mimid-96tt)
concludes that the call room IS the answer to the keying question rather
than an incidental example. mls-extensions §4.4's exported secret is
computable by every group member, so a call keyed from a room's
exporter is readable by every member of that room; making the call its
own group is what confines the keys to the participants. So the
call-room shape is load-bearing, and the strict-subset rule blocks its
commonest case.

THE PR: two small edits to draft-ietf-mimi-room-policy.md, "strict
subset" to "subset" and a clause exempting parent-dependent rooms from
the single-room rule, with the existing #40 as the rationale and a line
on why the call keying makes it matter. Keep it to the diff and the
reasoning; the WG reads short PRs.

Read the repo's CONTRIBUTING before posting, per the peer-contributing
rules. Posting needs Mark's own OK.
notes:

WHY IT IS WORTH SAYING AT ALL: #40 argues the change as an internal
inconsistency and #43 proposes the fix, and neither gives the keying
reason. Mark's own statement of it is on #59, which he closed as a
duplicate of #43, so a reader of #40 or #43 does not see it. Checked:
0 em-dashes, 0 bold, no mention of JMAP, 207 words.

----- the comment, verbatim -----

#40 argues this as an inconsistency between Section 5 and the note at
L274. The substantive reason is keying, which neither #40 nor this PR
gives.

Keying a call from a room's exported secret requires the call to have a
room of its own. draft-ietf-mls-extensions Section 4.4's
SafeExportSecret takes a ComponentID and nothing else, and its root is
derived from the group's epoch_secret, so every member of the group can
compute a component's secret for an epoch. Entitlement to a call's media
cannot be established by further derivation, because any derivation an
application performs on that secret is equally computable by every
member. It can only be established by the membership of the group the
secret comes from.

So a call keyed this way has its own parent-dependent room whose
participants are the call's participants. When everyone in the parent
room is on the call those two sets are equal, and Section 5's strict
subset forbids the room. That is the commonest call in a small room.

I have written this up as draft-atwood-mimi-calls, not submitted:
https://github.com/MarkAtwood/ietf-mimi-calls. Its section on the call's
own room assumes a subset rather than a strict subset, and depends on
this change or on the rewording this PR offers as an alternative.

----- end -----

Alternative destination if preferred: issue #40, so the motivation sits
with the problem statement rather than the proposed fix.
